clue.text: Here person in pain could have been on stretcher

definitions.text: Here person in pain could have been on stretcher

blocks.clueFragment: Here person in pain could have been on stretcher
blocks.note: surface reading: a patient in agony who might have been carried on a hospital stretcher
setter's reading: a stretcher is a device that stretches a body, the rack of an old dungeon

explanation.walkthrough: The stretcher here is not an ambulance one but the rack, on which victims were stretched; 'Here' points to the place where that happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon room for inflicting agony on prisoners, where the rack and similar devices were kept.

clue.text: Moving music from gypsies

explanation.surface: Stirring tunes played by Romany musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic peoples such as Romany and Irish Travellers are collectively called by this phrase in Britain.

clue.text: Fellow with an Australian pick-up in red is disproved

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the colour word that follows

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a ute is the Australian word for a pick-up truck

explanation.surface: Somebody's claim is knocked down because a man owns a red Aussie truck.
explanation.walkthrough: A ute, short for utility vehicle, is the everyday Australian name for a pick-up truck.
explanation.definitionFit: To refute a claim is to prove it false, so the past participle matches a statement shown wrong.

clue.text: Emphasise where sleepers should be placed

blocks.note: first meaning: to stress, as by drawing a rule beneath words
second meaning, read cryptically: railway sleepers lie beneath the track

explanation.walkthrough: Sleepers suggest people in bed, but here they are the timber beams laid under a railway track, so read the answer as UNDER LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing a stroke beneath text gives it stress, hence the verb for highlighting or stressing a point.

clue.text: Not many men face taking picture

indicators.note: many is M, the Roman thousand, and 'not' tells you to leave that letter out of the next word

blocks.note: a literary word for the face

explanation.surface: Few men are willing to face having their photo taken.
explanation.walkthrough: M stands for many because it is the Roman numeral for a thousand; 'picture' is a verb here, not a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, which is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: Container with a lid on the inside?

definitions.text: Container with a lid on the inside?

blocks.clueFragment: Container with a lid on the inside?
blocks.note: surface reading: a box oddly built with its cover inside rather than on top
setter's reading: lid is slang for a hat, so the box holds headwear

explanation.walkthrough: A lid on a container should be on top; slang 'lid' for headgear turns it into the thing kept inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A round case made for storing headwear, the item informally called a lid.

clue.text: Frame picture of horse?

blocks.note: first meaning: to set a picture on a card backing or in a frame
second meaning: an animal to ride

explanation.surface: Put a painting of a horse into a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers fixing artwork on a backing board, and the noun is a rider's horse or steed.

clue.text: During sex-change nurse gets presents

indicators.note: a change in the word before it means its letters get rearranged
during puts one thing in the middle of another, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to nurse is to tend or care for

explanation.surface: A nurse is given gifts during a patient's gender reassignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presents' looks like a noun for gifts, but it is a verb, as when one offers a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an invitation or thanks is to offer or present it, so both verbs mean offering.

clue.text: Studying good girls - useful for improving your looks?

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Reading about good-looking girls as a beauty tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks' seems to mean appearance, but it means the act of looking: these spectacles improve your sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles for close work make what you look at clearer, playfully improving the quality of your gaze.

clue.text: Fat diva, if off to make a legal declaration

indicators.note: off as in gone bad or out of order, so the preceding words are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A plump opera singer storms off to give a sworn statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A written statement sworn on oath for use as evidence in court is the formal legal declaration.

clue.text: BBC head goes free

indicators.note: the head going means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: Auntie is the nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: The Director-General of the BBC is released.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is affectionately called Auntie in Britain; drop its first letter to get UNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo knots or bonds is to set loose or release, the verb sense of free.

clue.text: Join hospital department engineers in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so this word is read right to left

explanation.surface: Retired engineers sign up to work for a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps; ENT is ear, nose and throat.
explanation.definitionFit: To join a competition or a profession is to enter it; both mean becoming part of something.

clue.text: Tenor performing in hut gets cut

indicators.note: the word before it is put through its paces and comes out in another order
one item is placed inside the other

explanation.surface: A singer giving a show in a hut finds his act trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made briefer has been cut down in length; both describe reduction.

clue.text: Sling dog into temporary accommodation

indicators.note: the words before are turned into something else, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Throwing the dog into a kennel or boarding house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sling' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'into' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Rented rooms in someone else's house are a short-term place to stay.

clue.text: Said you do wrong to go back on agreement

indicators.note: said means we want how the next word is pronounced, not how it is written
going back tells you to read the preceding word from right to left

blocks.note: the letter sounds just like the pronoun
to sin is to do wrong

explanation.surface: Saying you will go back on a deal is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: U, then SIN reversed to NIS, then ON: UNISON.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in unison means acting together in harmony, which is a state of accord.

clue.text: Thing transported by driver could be for an entertainer

definitions.note: the phrase describes a place rather than naming one, fair because the clue's 'could be' signals a loose description: a venue meant for performers

indicators.note: transported means carried off or moved about, so these letters are relocated

blocks.note: a driver is a golf club

explanation.surface: Some item a chauffeur carries might be meant for a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver is not a chauffeur but the golf club used off the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-night venue with music and cabaret is a place where singers and comedians perform.

clue.text: Both he and me turned into a huge person

indicators.note: the words are turned round and transformed into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Two people together have become one giant.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a biblical beast, the word is used for anything, or anyone, of enormous size.

clue.text: Depression returns to the Franco-Italian city

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a pan is a hollow in the ground, as in a salt pan

explanation.surface: A slump sends someone home to a city on the French-Italian border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Franco-Italian' looks like one adjective, but 'the Franco' is French 'the', LES, leaving 'Italian city' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern port at the foot of Vesuvius is a major city of Italy, Napoli to its people.

clue.text: Vegetable from an average crop

blocks.note: par is the standard or average level
to crop is to snip or cut short

explanation.surface: A vegetable gathered from a so-so harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' looks like a harvest, matching the vegetable, but it is the verb meaning cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale root grown in gardens and eaten roasted, related to the carrot.

clue.text: Hard worm taken by gannet, an insectivore

blocks.note: H for hard, as on pencils
to worm your way is to edge along
a gannet is slang for a greedy eater, a hog

explanation.surface: A tough worm is swallowed by a seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: The worm and the gannet look like prey and predator, but both are verbs and nicknames: worm means edge, and gannet is British slang for a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: This spiny garden mammal eats beetles, slugs and other small creatures, so it is classed among insect-eaters.

clue.text: Landlord detailed to go with girl gives a joyful shout

indicators.note: de-tailed means having the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a pub landlord is the host

explanation.surface: A publican assigned to accompany a young woman lets out a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' seems to mean assigned to a duty; read it as de-tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of praise or adoration to God, used in worship and on Palm Sunday.

clue.text: An ordered system in a disco's most unusual!

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Finding order in a nightclub would be remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' hints at an anagram, but the letters run straight across disco's most.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe seen as a harmonious, well-ordered whole, as opposed to chaos.

clue.text: For mineral he's moving into a coastal area

indicators.note: moving letters around rearranges the word in front
into places one piece inside the others

explanation.surface: A prospector heads to the beach in search of minerals.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip of shore between high and low tide, or the land next to the sea.

clue.text: Many standing round job centre looking for a seat

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word reads from bottom to top
the centre of a word is its middle letter
going round something means surrounding it

explanation.surface: A crowd stands around the Jobcentre hoping for somewhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jobcentre is a British state employment office; here 'job centre' is just the middle letter of job.
explanation.definitionFit: A backless seat for one person, with legs but no arms.

clue.text: She returns something useful

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A woman gives back a handy item.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessa is a girl's given name, so any woman called that can be referred to as 'she'.

clue.text: Having brought nothing back, try tongue

indicators.note: back tells you to read the word for nothing in the other direction

blocks.note: to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Having returned empty-handed, have a go at speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and the informal word for a foreign or specialist language is this one.

clue.text: Writing about poor Orlando Heath

indicators.note: poor means in a bad state, so the name after it is broken up and rearranged
about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: MS is manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An article about poor Orlando Heath, as though he were a person.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath looks like a surname with Orlando, but it is the definition: open uncultivated land.
explanation.definitionFit: A heath is open, uncultivated upland covered with heather and grass, the same terrain.

clue.text: Engineer passes bill, then discloses something confidential

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the following letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An engineer gets a bill through, then leaks a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for revealing a secret, often carelessly, means exactly letting confidential information out.
